title: Post-commit coding-agent host event observation policy
authority: TraceDecay host and application settlement authority

sensitivity.admission_rule: Secret and unadmitted personal data never cross the provider boundary; admitted payloads carry a privacy classification and redaction result.

relevance.admission_rule: Admit only bounded coding outcomes whose relevance is evidenced by the settled event; classify transient operational output as noise.

coding_scope_derivation.algorithm: Copy the exact identity fields from the already validated ScopeAdmissionReceiptV1 attached to the host or application event; verify its resolved-scope digest and session binding, and never parse a path, CWD, repository name, process ID, or nearest project to invent scope.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Copy source authority, event identity, revision, digest, and the canonical settlement receipt from the owning host or application authority; verify that the receipt binds the settled digest and commit point, and treat paths and ranges as evidence anchors only, never as source identity.

admission_requirements: The event is a completed or committed coding outcome, not an intent or preview.
The canonical source authority has emitted a settlement receipt before provider fan-out.
The exact scope receipt supplies profile, project, repository, worktree, branch, session, and resolved-scope-digest identity.
The source provenance receipt supplies authority, event ID, revision, digest, and settlement proof.
The event is classified for durability, sensitivity, and coding relevance.
Secret-like and unadmitted personal content is rejected or redacted before admission.
Provider delivery is advisory and cannot alter the settled source outcome.

default_exclusion_reasons.description: A request, plan, preview, or proposed action has not produced a settled coding outcome.
The source authority reports that the attempted mutation was reverted or did not remain committed.
Content exists only in an editor, overlay, temporary buffer, or pending transaction.
The payload contains raw credentials, secret material, or a secret-like value that is not redacted.
The event is an in-flight lifecycle signal, heartbeat, cancellation, or temporary snapshot.
The event is operational or read-only noise with no bounded coding outcome to teach.
The operation ended without a definitive committed or completed result.
The authoritative exact coding scope is absent, stale, or inconsistent.
The owning authority cannot provide a stable source identity and canonical settlement proof.
The signal describes provider delivery or infrastructure state rather than a host coding outcome.

host_families.notes: A provider observation follows the durable session observation commit, not an incoming hook intent.

host_families.event_surface: rollout JSONL frames and app-server records
host_families.notes: The resolved project or profile admission owns the rollout; a path is never used as source identity.
Only a complete normalized snapshot admitted by the host authority can leave the session boundary.
SQLite row identity and the durable session scope are evidence; ambient database paths are not identity.
Snapshot completion and canonical admission are required before a provider can observe the record.
A settled native row is normalized under the authoritative project/profile route before fan-out.
The source generation and snapshot order are ordering evidence, while scope comes from admission.
Only normalized, privacy-classified, durably admitted records are eligible.
Session status and LSP notifications are not observations unless the owning authority settles a coding outcome.
Host-specific wire details remain in the adapter; the observation boundary remains provider-neutral.

event_coverage.coverage_basis: All supported coding-agent host session surfaces and TraceDecay application outcome boundaries that can produce a durable coding signal are represented; an event not listed here is excluded by the unclassified rule.

event_classes.summary: A normalized user or assistant session message has been durably admitted by the host session authority.

canonical_commit_point.settled_state: ObservationPersistOutcome::Committed with a durable observation ID and cursor advance
canonical_commit_point.ordering_authority: The source cursor and generation supplied by the host adapter, not wall-clock arrival time.
canonical_commit_point.provider_fanout: Only after durable session observation commit and privacy settlement.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Copy the exact scope identity from the validated admission receipt; never parse a path or CWD to infer a project or worktree.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Copy and verify the host settlement receipt and source digest; paths and byte ranges remain evidence anchors only.

payload_policy.notes: A message is advisory provider input, never an accepted Native fact by itself.

event_classes.summary: A tool invocation has reached a typed terminal result and any source effect has a committed-effect receipt.

canonical_commit_point.settled_state: DispatchExecutionSettlement joined with a typed terminal outcome and committed-effect state
canonical_commit_point.ordering_authority: The operation settlement receipt and its source sequence, not request-start or response-arrival time.
canonical_commit_point.provider_fanout: Only after the canonical tool result is settled; provider failure cannot change the tool result.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Copy scope fields from the operation's validated admission receipt and require its resolved scope digest to match exactly; never infer scope from a tool argument or path string.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Use the typed terminal settlement and committed-effect receipt as source provenance; do not turn a requested tool call into a settled event.

payload_policy.notes: A failed terminal result can be useful evidence when it is settled; a started or cancelled request is not.

event_classes.summary: An authorized source edit has atomically published bytes in the exact worktree and emitted a settlement receipt.

canonical_commit_point.settled_state: Atomic publication succeeded and expected file identity/generation was advanced
canonical_commit_point.ordering_authority: The source-edit publication generation and after digest, not editor-buffer time.
canonical_commit_point.provider_fanout: Only after atomic source publication; a later rollback is a separate excluded event.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Use the scope receipt selected before publication and bind the edit receipt to its worktree ID; never parse the edited file path to select scope.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Derive source identity from the atomic publication receipt, before/after digests, and source revision; retain paths only as evidence anchors.

payload_policy.notes: The current worktree remains canonical; the provider receives an advisory outcome projection.

event_classes.summary: A test or verification command has completed with a durable result tied to the exact source generation.

canonical_commit_point.authority: TraceDecay test execution and result authority
canonical_commit_point.settled_state: Test process reached a typed terminal result and result receipt was durably recorded
canonical_commit_point.ordering_authority: Execution receipt and source generation, not process-start or log-line order.
canonical_commit_point.provider_fanout: Only after the test result is terminal and durably recorded.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Copy exact scope from the test execution admission receipt and bind it to the source generation; never infer project scope from a test path.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Use the terminal test receipt, source generation, and result digest as provenance; an unfinished process has no admissible source event.

payload_policy.notes: Failure is a settled coding signal; it is not a source edit and cannot be rewritten by a provider.

event_classes.summary: A diagnostic broker has committed a complete bounded snapshot for a known source generation.

canonical_commit_point.settled_state: Complete snapshot is committed and bound to a source generation
canonical_commit_point.ordering_authority: Snapshot ID and source generation, not debounce arrival order.
canonical_commit_point.provider_fanout: Only after complete snapshot settlement; partial/unavailable snapshots remain operational evidence.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Copy the exact scope attached to the diagnostic snapshot authority and bind its source generation; never derive project identity from a document URI.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Use the committed snapshot receipt and digest as provenance; an in-flight debounced update is not a source event.

payload_policy.notes: Diagnostic content is evidence about code health, not permission to mutate code or Native facts.

event_classes.summary: The exact worktree's Git authority has observed and settled a commit object for the admitted coding scope.

canonical_commit_point.authority: Git reference authority for the exact admitted worktree
canonical_commit_point.settled_state: Commit object and ref observation are verified against the admitted repository/worktree
canonical_commit_point.ordering_authority: The Git commit graph and exact ref, not file mtime or branch display text.
canonical_commit_point.provider_fanout: Only after Git evidence is verified; branch/status polling remains excluded noise.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Copy repository, worktree, branch, session, and resolved scope digest from the validated scope and Git route receipts; never derive identity from a path or branch label.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Derive source identity from the verified commit object, ref receipt, parent set, and source digest; Git paths remain evidence only.

payload_policy.notes: A Git commit is evidence of a committed coding outcome; a status poll is not.

event_classes.summary: An explicitly authorized promotion has passed Native validation and durably settled in the Native fact authority.

canonical_commit_point.settled_state: Validated promotion committed with lineage, idempotency, and privacy receipt
canonical_commit_point.ordering_authority: Native fact log commit and lineage receipt, not a provider proposal timestamp.
canonical_commit_point.provider_fanout: Only after explicit Native promotion; provider recall cannot implicitly promote a fact.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Copy scope from the Native owner receipt and retain provider scope as evidence only; never infer ownership from a database path.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Use the explicit promotion operation, Native lineage, and privacy receipt as source provenance; a provider candidate is not a settled promotion.

payload_policy.notes: This observes an authorized Native settlement; it does not grant a cognitive provider Native authority.

event_classes.summary: A user or system feedback outcome has been durably recorded with its bounded target and result.

canonical_commit_point.settled_state: Feedback source event and resulting trust/outcome transition are durably recorded
canonical_commit_point.ordering_authority: Feedback log settlement and target identity, not UI preview order.
canonical_commit_point.provider_fanout: Only after feedback is settled; provider output cannot rewrite Native feedback.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Copy exact scope from the feedback authority's admission receipt; never use a UI route, path, or display label to infer coding scope.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Use the settled feedback source event and transition digest; previews and unsubmitted controls have no canonical provenance.

payload_policy.notes: Feedback is an outcome signal and remains separate from source code and Native fact authority.

event_classes.summary: A TraceDecay automation run has reached a durable typed outcome tied to its admitted coding scope.

canonical_commit_point.settled_state: Run ledger contains a terminal outcome, input/evidence identity, and any committed effect receipt
canonical_commit_point.ordering_authority: Automation run ledger settlement and run identity, not scheduler intent or heartbeat timing.
canonical_commit_point.provider_fanout: Only after the automation outcome is settled and privacy-checked.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Copy exact scope from the automation run's admission receipt, including its resolved scope digest, and bind it to the settled run identity; never infer scope from a scheduler path or job label.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Use the terminal automation receipt and input/effect digests as provenance; a scheduled or running job is not a source event.

payload_policy.notes: Automation observation is operational evidence and cannot silently mutate canonical code or facts.

event_classes.summary: A host recorded an intention or request to invoke a tool before execution settled.

exclusion_reason.description: Tool intent can be edited, denied, cancelled, or superseded before any coding effect exists.

scope_derivation.algorithm: No provider observation is formed; exclude the intent before scope binding.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: No settled source receipt exists; exclude rather than guess provenance.

payload_policy.notes: Intent is not a committed coding outcome.

event_classes.summary: A tool worker started but has not produced a terminal result.

exclusion_reason.description: An in-flight worker may fail or be cancelled and has no settled effect.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude the lifecycle signal before scope binding; await a terminal settlement event.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: No canonical settlement receipt exists for a started worker.

payload_policy.notes: Provider delivery cannot observe execution progress.

event_classes.summary: An edit was proposed or previewed but has not atomically published bytes.

exclusion_reason.description: Editor and preview state is mutable and may never become current worktree truth.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude proposed bytes before scope binding and before provider fan-out.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: A preview has no canonical source settlement receipt; do not derive provenance from its path.

payload_policy.notes: Only a successful atomic publication can be observed.

event_classes.summary: A previously attempted edit was rolled back or failed to remain committed.

exclusion_reason.description: Rolled-back bytes are not current coding truth and must never be taught as a provider observation.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude rollback evidence before forming any provider scope envelope.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: The rollback receipt is an exclusion reason, not an admissible source settlement.

payload_policy.notes: Rollback is explicit negative evidence and does not cross the provider boundary.

event_classes.summary: A source buffer or temporary file changed without a durable source-edit commit.

exclusion_reason.description: Uncommitted state is not authoritative and may be discarded by the host or editor.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude the buffer change before scope binding; wait for an atomic source-edit settlement.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: No committed source digest or settlement receipt exists.

payload_policy.notes: This is the explicit default for editor and overlay state.

event_classes.summary: A test run was requested but no result has settled.

exclusion_reason.description: A request does not establish whether the test ran, passed, or produced a coding signal.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude the request before scope binding and await a terminal result receipt.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: A requested test has no settled source event.

payload_policy.notes: Only terminal test outcomes are eligible.

event_classes.summary: A test run stopped without a definitive completed result.

exclusion_reason.description: An aborted test cannot establish a completed coding result and may only reflect cancellation or infrastructure loss.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude an incomplete run before provider scope binding.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: No terminal source settlement is available for an aborted run.

payload_policy.notes: Infrastructure or cancellation noise stays out of the provider observation stream.

event_classes.summary: A debounced, partial, stale, or in-flight diagnostic update has not settled as a complete snapshot.

exclusion_reason.description: Intermediate diagnostic updates are superseded by later snapshots and have no stable source generation.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude the update before scope binding; a complete snapshot may be considered separately.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: No canonical snapshot settlement receipt exists.

payload_policy.notes: Only a complete bounded diagnostic snapshot can be relevant evidence.

event_classes.summary: A branch, status, or working-tree poll was observed without a settled commit outcome.

exclusion_reason.description: Polling output is mutable context and cannot prove a committed coding outcome.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude polling output before scope binding; a verified commit event has its own policy row.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: A status poll has no canonical settlement receipt.

payload_policy.notes: Git commit evidence is admitted only through the separate settled commit event.

event_classes.summary: A host emitted a heartbeat, keepalive, or progress marker without a new coding outcome.

exclusion_reason.description: Keepalive activity is operational noise and has no durable lesson.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude heartbeat noise before scope binding.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Heartbeat has no canonical coding settlement receipt.

payload_policy.notes: Operational liveness is not provider learning input.

event_classes.summary: A provider generated an advisory recall candidate without an explicit Native promotion or host coding settlement.

exclusion_reason.description: Provider recall is advisory output, not a TraceDecay host source event or canonical coding outcome.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Do not form a provider observation from provider recall output.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Provider output cannot mint a canonical source receipt.

payload_policy.notes: Recall candidates remain advisory and are handled by the recall contract.

event_classes.summary: A fact proposal exists without explicit Native validation and durable promotion.

exclusion_reason.description: A proposal is not a Native fact and may be rejected, edited, or superseded before promotion.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude proposals before scope binding and wait for explicit Native promotion.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: A proposal has no canonical promotion settlement receipt.

payload_policy.notes: Native promotion is a separate admitted event only after its own authority commits.

event_classes.summary: A feedback control was previewed or drafted but not submitted and settled.

exclusion_reason.description: A preview does not establish user intent or a durable feedback outcome.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude a feedback preview before scope binding.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: No settled feedback source receipt exists.

payload_policy.notes: Only submitted and settled feedback can be observed.

event_classes.summary: An automation run was scheduled or queued but has not reached a terminal outcome.

exclusion_reason.description: Scheduling does not prove that automation ran or changed coding state.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude scheduling intent before scope binding; a settled run has its own event class.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: A scheduled job has no terminal source settlement receipt.

payload_policy.notes: Only a settled automation outcome can leave the application boundary.

event_classes.summary: A host payload contains raw secret material or unadmitted personal data before privacy-safe redaction.

exclusion_reason.description: Raw credentials and unadmitted personal data are never provider observation input, whether or not the surrounding event settled.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Reject secret-bearing content before binding any provider scope or payload.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Do not derive or persist source provenance for a raw secret payload; a sanitized replacement must produce a new admitted event.

payload_policy.notes: Secret classification is fail-closed and cannot be bypassed by a commit claim.

event_classes.summary: A provider delivery receipt records dispatch state but is not a host or application coding source event.

exclusion_reason.description: Provider delivery state belongs to the observation contract's operational receipts and must not recursively become a source observation.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Do not recursively observe provider delivery receipts.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: Provider receipts cannot mint a canonical host source event.

payload_policy.notes: Keep provider delivery evidence in the provider contract and operations ledger.

event_classes.summary: A read-only source or metadata operation completed without a source mutation or durable coding outcome.

exclusion_reason.description: Read completion is common transient activity and does not establish a committed coding outcome by itself.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude read-only completion before provider scope binding.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: A read result does not provide a canonical coding settlement receipt.

payload_policy.notes: Source reads may support a later committed outcome but are not observations themselves.

event_classes.summary: A host prepared a compaction or summary preview that has not become a settled session record.

exclusion_reason.description: A compaction preview is replaceable derived text until the host commits a session record.

scope_derivation.algorithm: Exclude preview text before scope binding; only a committed session message can be admitted.

source_provenance_derivation.algorithm: No canonical session settlement receipt exists for a preview.

payload_policy.notes: Derived previews do not cross the provider boundary.

invariants: Only completed or committed coding outcomes may be admitted to provider observation fan-out.
Every admitted event names one canonical commit point owned by TraceDecay or the exact admitted worktree authority.
Every excluded event carries a typed reason and is excluded before provider scope binding or payload dispatch.
Speculative tool intent, proposed edits, rolled-back mutations, and uncommitted buffers never become observations.
Raw secrets and unadmitted personal data are fail-closed regardless of whether a surrounding operation settled.
Exact profile, project, repository, worktree, branch, session, and resolved-scope digest come from an authoritative receipt, never path parsing.

The resolved-scope digest is content identity for one admitted scope and is compared only for exact equality; it is never an ordering revision, version counter, watermark, or freshness signal, and a mismatch excludes the event instead of selecting a newer scope.
Replay and admission ordering come only from the source event revision, source cursor, and source generation supplied by the owning authority, never from the resolved-scope digest.
Source authority, event ID, revision, digest, and canonical settlement receipt come from the owning authority, while paths are evidence anchors only.
Unknown host or application events follow the default exclusion rule and require an explicit unclassified reason before any scope is bound.
Provider latency, failure, or advisory output cannot alter canonical code, session, Native facts, tools, approvals, or settled source outcomes.
A later settled event may be admitted after an excluded intent or transient, but the excluded event itself is never retroactively replayed.
